notes:
- Creator pages show their works again: The staff profile asked AniList for `staffMedia` but the model read `media`, so the field was always null and every creator's work row was empty. The response is now mapped to the right field, duplicate credits for one title collapse to one poster, and the row keeps the role the person is known for instead of whichever credit AniList listed first.
- Works come before the biography: A long bio pushed the one row a creator page exists for below the fold. The rows now sit above the biography, and a creator's heading reads "Worked on" instead of "Appears in".
- Music videos appear on their shows again: AniList attaches a song through a CHARACTER relation, which the relation row treated as a crossover and removed. Music videos are now kept, labelled "Music video", and placed before a long show's specials.
- Manga relations carry their length: Relation cards read only `episodes`, so a manga card silently lost its count. Chapters, or volumes when chapters are unknown, now sit beside the format, and a manga page's row reads "Volumes & Relations".
- Relations cannot mix up an anime and a manga: The row deduplicated by id alone, and the detail map was keyed the same way, so a manga sharing a number with an anime could inherit its poster and synopsis. Both now compare the namespace as well as the id.
- The full-screen cover fits the artwork: The viewer was a fixed 340x440 window, which letterboxed every 2:3 cover and used guessed pan limits. The frame now follows the image's own aspect ratio and the pan bounds come from its measured size.
- Covers start loading sooner: The image client left OkHttp's five-requests-per-host default, so a twelve-card row downloaded five covers at a time. The pool and dispatcher are now sized for a wall of posters, with warm connections kept across a scroll.
- The parent's cover keeps its shape: The small cover in the prequel/parent card was a cropped 48dp square; it is now a 48dp-wide 2:3 poster like every other cover in the app.
